content:
A listener writes “I thought I would share my paranormal stories with you. I worked for the Postal Service for over 30 years, and these experiences happened a few years before I retired.

I was working for the Postal Service in California as an Express Mail courier. I drove a staff car, delivering and picking up Express Mail every day. My route took me through Fresno, Madera, Chowchilla, Los Banos, Santa Rita, Dos Palos, Firebaugh, Mendota, and Kerman before I returned to Madera and Fresno. It was more than 200 miles of driving every day, and I loved it.

One day, after arriving at the post office in Madera, California, I had some time to kill before getting back on the road. I had a schedule to maintain, so I couldn’t leave too early or too late. I decided to sit in the break room, where employees would take their breaks and eat lunch.

I sat down and began reading a newspaper while two women chatted nearby. As I read, something caught my attention. I pretended to keep reading, but I was actually listening to their conversation.

One woman said, “This guy was wearing his postal uniform, just sitting there rocking back and forth. So I said hi to him, but he didn’t respond. As I turned away, I asked a question, and when I turned back, he was gone. It wasn’t even two seconds.”

As I listened to her tell the other woman what had happened, I thought to myself, Wow, a ghost! I even chuckled a little to myself.

But then she began describing the man to her coworker.

“He just sat there rocking back and forth. He had a full beard and curly or wavy dark hair.”

When I heard that description, I immediately perked up. I didn’t say anything, but I thought to myself, Hmm, that sounds a lot like my brother.

My brother, Ralph, was killed on December 22, 1984. He was wearing his postal uniform when he died, and he had worked at that very post office.

I decided that when I got home, I would look for a photograph of my brother and bring it with me the following day.

When I got home, I found a picture of him and brought it to work the next morning.

After arriving at the Madera post office and taking care of my duties, I looked around for the woman I had overheard the day before. I couldn’t find her and was getting ready to leave when she suddenly came around the corner.

I stopped her and said, “Hi. Do you remember yesterday, when you were talking with your friend in the break room about the guy you saw sitting in the chair who suddenly disappeared?”

She replied, “Oh, yes! And it wasn’t just me. Other people have seen him here over the years, too. It’s always the same guy. I’ve only worked here for a few years.”

I reached into my pocket, pulled out my brother’s photograph, held it up for her to see, and asked, “Is this the man you saw?”

There was no hesitation. She didn’t study the photograph or take time to contemplate whether it was the same person. She looked at it, and I watched the color drain from her face.

“Oh my God! That’s him!” she exclaimed.

I told her that the man in the photograph was my brother, who had been killed in 1984 while wearing his postal uniform.

I thought she was going to collapse right there. The experience upset her so much that she became physically ill and had to go home from work.

Understand that no one there knew who I was. I had never met anyone at that post office before, as I was brand-new to the job. My brother and I also had different last names.

How is something like that possible?

These are mysteries we may never fully understand. All we can do is speculate.

I have another experience that happened about a year later, which I will share after the account of my retirement.

The Mysterious Object

The third mysterious experience of my life happened in 2010. My wife and I had retired and were living in Oakhurst, California. We were preparing to move back to Clovis, California, to take care of my father.

The town just before Oakhurst is called Coarsegold. Both towns are located in the mountains, about seven miles apart and not far from Yosemite National Park.

Coarsegold has an area where people gather to sell household goods, products, and crafts. It’s similar to a flea market, where vendors set up their stalls, sell their belongings, and enjoy spending time together.

In August 2010, I took some items from home to sell because we were preparing to move back to Clovis.

I made arrangements to spend a few nights in the area so I could get there early the following morning. I spoke with several other vendors and told them I would be sleeping in my car to keep an eye on my belongings. Some of them asked if I would also watch over their merchandise if they left it there overnight. Of course, I was happy to help.

That Friday night, I had just finished talking on my cell phone with my friend Richard. It was around 10:30 p.m., and I had backed my Dodge Durango into an open area beside a large grassy field.

After ending the call, I spread out my sleeping bag in the back of the Durango. I checked the front area, where everyone’s merchandise was set up, and everything looked fine. There didn’t appear to be anyone around.

For no particular reason, I decided to look out the back of my Durango and across the field, even though there was nothing back there except grass.

As I looked out, I noticed an object about the size of a large beach ball. It wasn’t a beach ball, though. It had a metallic appearance. From what I can remember, its surface was completely smooth, and it was no more than about 30 feet away from me.

The strangest thing was that it was hovering approximately two feet above the ground.

I thought to myself, What in the world is that?

Almost as soon as the thought crossed my mind, the object began moving across the field while maintaining the same height above the ground. It looked as though it were searching for something or surveying the area.

To say I was mesmerized would be an understatement. It never even occurred to me to take out my phone and try to record a video.

The object moved toward the center of the open area. It had a faint glow, but it wasn’t bright like the lights people often describe when reporting unexplained objects or glowing spheres. Instead, it had a dull, metallic-looking glow.

Then, suddenly, it shot upward to a height of approximately 20 to 30 feet and stopped.

Just as quickly, it descended and began moving across the field again.

When it did that, it scared the hell out of me. I’ll leave it at that, except to say that I had chills running through my body.

I retrieved my high-powered flashlight and my .38-caliber revolver from the glove compartment. When I returned to the window, the object was still there, moving around.

I took my flashlight and shone it directly at the object. I’m not sure I can adequately describe what happened next.

The light did not reflect off the object at all.

It was as though the object had no reflective surface whatsoever. In fact, it looked as if the light were disappearing into a hole, never returning or illuminating anything. Perhaps the object wasn’t really there in the way I understood it to be. All I knew was that it wasn’t reflecting light as an ordinary physical object would.

The beam seemed to disappear into the object, almost like a black spot in space. The portions of the beam that missed it continued illuminating the surrounding grass and ground normally.

Shortly afterward, the object shot upward again to a height of about 20 to 30 feet and stopped. Then, in the blink of an eye, it took off and disappeared from sight.

There was no sound. Nothing at all.

I didn’t sleep for the next few nights. I still had one more night to spend in the area, and I kept thinking about what I had witnessed.

I told myself that if it returned the following night, I would get out of my car and try to get closer to it. Of course, I planned to take my .38-caliber revolver with me.

Looking back, perhaps I was lucky that it never returned.

What I didn’t know at the time was that, that very same weekend, there were several UFO sightings in the Fresno and Clovis, California, area, approximately 30 miles away. The sightings were reportedly covered extensively in local news throughout the valley.

I don’t know whether these experiences would be of interest to your program, but there’s no pressure. Keep doing what you’re doing. Your show provides an outlet for people who have experienced unusual events in their lives and need a place to share their stories.

I believe your program can be therapeutic for people who have gone through experiences they cannot explain. Sometimes, simply having someone willing to listen can make all the difference.”
